# Step 1: Laying groundwork

## Step 1a: Loading packages

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Step 1b: Loading tidy data back in

```{r}
# age participation
age_participation <- read.csv("~/Desktop/independent proj/data/processed/age_participation.csv")

glimpse(age_participation)

# gender participation
gender_participation <- read.csv("~/Desktop/independent proj/data/processed/gender_participation.csv")

# stopping rates
stopping_rates <- read.csv("~/Desktop/independent proj/data/processed/stopping_rates.csv")
```

# Step 2: Basic line plots

## Step 2a: Age group

```{r}
age_participation %>%
  filter(sector == "Overall") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = participation_rate, color = age_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Workplace pension participation by age group (2009-2025)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Participation rate",
    color = "Age group"
  )
```

## Step 2b: Gender

```{r}
gender_participation %>%
  filter(sector == "Overall") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = participation_rate, color = gender)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Workplace pension participation by gender (2009-2025)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Participation rate",
    color = "Gender"
  )
```

## Step 2c: Stopping rates

```{r}
stopping_rates %>%
  filter(section == "Overall") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = quarter_index, y = stopping_rate)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = "Stopping saving (opt-out) rate among AE-eligible employees",
    x = "Quarter (1 = 2014-15 Q1, 47 = 2025-26 Q3)",
    y = "Stopping saving rate"
  )
```

# Step 4: Interrupted time series analysis (ITS)

## Step 4a: Building a clean yearly series to test on

```{r}
overall_trend <- age_participation %>%
  filter(sector == "Overall") %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(participation_rate = mean(participation_rate))

print(overall_trend)
```

## Step 4b: Creating policy variables

```{r}
overall_trend <- overall_trend %>%
  mutate(
    post = if_else(year >= 2012, 1, 0),
    year_centered = year - 2012
  )

print(overall_trend)
```

## Step 4c: Fitting the segmented regression

```{r}
its_model <- lm(participation_rate ~ year_centered * post, data = overall_trend)

summary(its_model)
```

# Step 5: Stopping-rate data

## Step 5a: Building a policy variable for the cost-of-living period

```{r}
# using quarter 29 as the cutoff
overall_stopping <- stopping_rates %>%
  filter(section == "Overall") %>%
  mutate(
    quarter_centered = quarter_index - 29,
    post_col = if_else(quarter_index >= 29, 1, 0)
  )

print(overall_stopping)
```

## Step 5b: Fitting the segmented regression on stopping rates

```{r}
its_stopping_model <- lm(stopping_rate ~ quarter_centered * post_col, data = overall_stopping)

summary(its_stopping_model)
```

# Step 6: Age-band stopping data

## Step 6a: Building age-band stopping data with same policy variables

```{r}
age_stopping <- stopping_rates %>%
  filter(section == "By Age Band") %>%
  mutate(
    quarter_centered = quarter_index - 29,
    post_col = if_else(quarter_index >= 29, 1, 0)
  )

print(age_stopping)
```

## Step 6b: Fitting a model that lets the effect differ by age band

```{r}
age_stopping_model <- lm(
  stopping_rate ~ quarter_centered * post_col * group,
  data = age_stopping
)

summary(age_stopping_model)
```
